target.title: fix(slack): validate redirect targets against Slack hostname allowlist (SSRF)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`fetchWithSlackAuth` in `extensions/slack/src/monitor/media.ts` validated the initial URL via `assertSlackFileUrl` (Slack hostname check), but then handed redirect handling to fetch's `redirect: "follow"` — which follows up to 20 hops to **any HTTPS URL** without re-checking the hostname. A redirect from a Slack host to an arbitrary endpoint (internal service, attacker host, cloud metadata) bypassed the SSRF guard entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old code only checked `resolvedUrl.protocol === "https:"` after the first redirect, then let `redirect: "follow"` take over. The sibling `createSlackMediaFetch` (same file) and the canonical `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts` both use `redirect: "manual"` with hostname validation. `fetchWithSlackAuth` was the inconsistent outlier.

The function has no prod caller today (prod Slack media uses `saveRemoteMedia` → canonical fetch-guard), but it is an exported public API. Fixing the SSRF shape now prevents a future caller from inheriting the bypass.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change (no prod caller). The exported `fetchWithSlackAuth` now safely bounds redirects to Slack hostnames, blocking SSRF via redirect if any future caller adopts it.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** `fetchWithSlackAuth` followed redirects to arbitrary HTTPS URLs (bypassing the Slack hostname check), enabling SSRF if the function were called from a message-handling path.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `94316d858f` on branch `fix/slack-fetch-auth-ssrf-redirect-guard`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-slack-ssrf.mjs` — imports the real `fetchWithSlackAuth`, installs a mock fetch (via `_isMockFunction` so `resolveSlackFetchForRuntime` picks it up), and exercises four cases: legit 200, non-Slack initial URL, redirect to non-Slack host, cross-origin Slack redirect.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  Terminal capture of node runtime verification (live stdout):
    fetchWithSlackAuth SSRF redirect guard

    [PASS] Slack URL + 200 -> status 200
    [PASS] non-Slack initial -> throw
    [PASS] redirect to non-Slack host -> throw (SSRF blocked)
    [PASS] cross-origin Slack redirect -> strip auth + follow (status 200, auth stripped: true)

  Verdict: PASS
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** A redirect to a non-Slack host (`internal.corp.example.com`) now throws instead of being followed. Cross-origin Slack redirects (`files.slack.com` to `cdn.slack-edge.com`) still succeed but strip the Authorization header. Legitimate non-redirect responses are unchanged.
- **What was not tested:** Live end-to-end against a real Slack file redirect (the function has no prod caller; the vitest suite covers the real class path with mocked fetch, and the node proof covers the SSRF decision boundary).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/slack/src/monitor/media.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
EXIT=0 (type check passed)
```

Added two SSRF regression tests: redirect to a non-Slack host throws, redirect to non-HTTPS throws. Updated existing redirect tests to expect `redirect: "manual"` on the second hop (the loop no longer hands off to `redirect: "follow"`).

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: No - the function has no prod caller; prod Slack media uses `saveRemoteMedia` with the canonical fetch-guard.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: Yes (improvement) - closes an SSRF bypass where redirects could reach arbitrary HTTPS hosts; every redirect hop is now re-validated against the Slack hostname allowlist and cross-origin hops strip Authorization.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No - internal helper in the Slack plugin; the function signature is unchanged.
- Highest-risk area: a future caller that relied on the old redirect-follow-to-anywhere behavior would break — but no such caller exists today, and the old behavior was a security bug.
- Mitigation: 45 media tests (incl. two new SSRF regression cases) + node runtime verification of all four redirect shapes + tsgo green.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)
